_about: Chapters of the FigJam board 'Digital services system', exported as images. The files are the source of truth and the board is drawn from them; these pictures illustrate the docs listed under each. 'system' means the /system page. Re-export a chapter when its file changes (see the table in ../../README.md).

chapters.title: The system on one page
chapters.caption: Eight steps run around one document, the roadmap. Steps 2 and 3 set direction; steps 4 to 8 do the work; what people say comes back in at step 1. Dashed lines show which roadmap section a step updates.
chapters.alt: Flow diagram. Eight green step boxes form a loop around a yellow box labelled Roadmap, which lists its five sections: vision and strategy, goal progress, Now Next Later grid, quarterly commitments, sprint report. Clockwise from the left: 1 Capture ideas (ongoing), 2 Set direction (yearly), 3 Plan the quarter (quarterly), 4 Discover (inside an Initiative), 5 Slice the work, 6 Build and release (sprints), 7 Review the sprint (every two weeks), 8 Enable (each launch). Under each step, what it makes. Dashed arrows run from Set direction to roadmap sections 1-2, from Plan the quarter to sections 3-4, and from Review the sprint to section 5. An arrow labelled feedback runs from Enable back to Capture ideas.

chapters.title: Set direction and plan the quarter
chapters.caption: What feeds the yearly direction review, what it produces, and how those artifacts feed the four quarterly planning sessions.
chapters.alt: Flow diagram in three columns. Left, four blue inputs: leadership priorities and mandates, user research and feedback, last year's goal progress, and patterns from the idea log. They point to the green step 2 Set direction (yearly direction review). It produces yellow artifacts: vision and strategy, and goals for 1 to 2 years. Those, plus the idea log, active Initiatives and their Solutions, the small request board, and last quarter's commitments, point to the green step 3 Plan the quarter (four sessions). It produces updated goal progress, new Initiatives, the Now Next Later grid, and the quarterly commitments (Deliverables, intended progress, capacity).

chapters.title: Inside an Initiative, until the outcome is reached
chapters.caption: Discover, decide, slice, build, enable, measure. If a Solution doesn't hold up, or the outcome isn't reached, the loop goes back to Discover with another Solution.
chapters.alt: Flow diagram, left to right. An Initiative (hypothesis and outcome measure) feeds step 4 Discover, which produces a discovery brief and an assumption log. A purple decision asks: Solution holds up? No loops back to Discover with another Solution; yes produces a Solution. Step 5 Slice the work produces a story map and Deliverables. Step 6 Build and release (sprints) produces user stories and release notes. Step 8 Enable produces an enable plan and readiness check, feedback to triage, and a Measure the outcome step that updates goal progress. A final decision asks: Outcome reached? Yes closes the Initiative; no goes back to Discover with another Solution.

chapters.title: One sprint, every two weeks
chapters.caption: Deliverables, ready stories and the small request board go into sprint planning; the sprint ends with a review, a sprint report and a retro.
chapters.alt: Flow diagram, left to right. Three inputs, Deliverables in Now, ready user stories, and the small request board, feed sprint planning, which sets a sprint goal and committed stories. Build, test and release runs alongside mid-sprint refinement, which readies stories for the next sprint. The sprint produces released changes and release notes. Step 7 Review the sprint produces the sprint report and commitment status, then a retro that updates the team working agreements.

chapters.title: Requests: how they are reviewed
chapters.caption: Every request gets an answer. Some join the roadmap, some are small work, some are a no. Bugs skip triage.
chapters.alt: Flow diagram. A submitted request goes to a weekly team triage review (within 5 business days) with five outcomes: already on the roadmap, link to the roadmap item; small request, add to the small request board; large or strategic, add to the idea log; idea for improvement, add to the idea log; will not do, close it. Every outcome ends with telling the requester. Ideas for improvement go to a product manager review at intake or quarterly planning with three results: mined into an Initiative; future consideration (not yes, not no, and we won't follow up); or closed with the reason. A separate row: a reported bug skips triage and goes to the technical architect, urgent fixes now, otherwise the technical maintenance list. Definitions of each outcome follow below the diagram.

chapters.title: What gets made
chapters.caption: Every artifact with a one-line definition and how it connects to the next. Epic is a dashed, optional link.
chapters.alt: Artifact map. Yellow cards, each with a name and one line: Roadmap (published quarterly, one document with five sections); Goal (1-2 years, a change in what people do with a starting value and target); Idea (ongoing, any suggestion from anyone); Initiative (open until the outcome is reached, the tracked bet that an opportunity will move a goal); Solution (one of several tried, tested, built, kept or dropped); Deliverable (committed this quarter, a tangible thing handed over); User story (the smallest piece of value, built in one sprint); Sprint report (each sprint); Release notes; Small request (ongoing, a bounded change under a sprint that does not advance a goal); Discovery brief; Assumption log; Launch readiness check; Enable plan. Labelled arrows connect them: Idea can become Initiative, Initiative is pursued by Solutions, a Solution is sliced into Deliverables, Deliverables are broken into user stories, and so on.

chapters.title: When it happens: team rhythm
chapters.caption: One example quarter, December to March, with a lane for each cadence: yearly, quarterly, monthly, sprints, ongoing.
chapters.alt: Timeline of one quarter across four months, December to March, in five lanes. Yearly: a direction review (vision, strategy, goals) in early December. Quarterly: quarterly planning (grid, commitments) in mid December, roadmap published in early January, next quarter planning in late March, quarter review (goal progress) at the end of March. Monthly: advisory and steering meetings in late January, February and March. Sprints: six two-week sprints from early January to the end of March, each ending in a sprint review that updates the sprint report. Ongoing: weekly request intake and discovery inside active Initiatives.
